On Christ's 'With desire I have desired to eat this passover with you before I suffer' (Lk 22:15), Cyril reads the Hebraic-redoubled-formula (epithymia epethymēsa) as the canonical Lukan anchor of the doctrine of Christ's deliberate-eager-anticipation of the institutional Last Supper: not reluctant, not pressured, but deeply-desired. The Lord's eagerness for the canonical-eucharistic-institution dignifies every later celebration. Tewahedo eucharistic theology cites Lk 22:15 as the canonical Lukan anchor of the doctrine of Christ's desire-for-the-eucharist; every Tewahedo Mass is participation in the Lord's own canonical-desire-fulfilment.

candidates.draft_body:
Cyril of Alexandria Commentary on Luke (c. 430 AD)

On Christ's word to the arresting-officers 'this is your hour, and the power of darkness' (Lk 22:53), Cyril reads the doubled-phrase (your-hour + power-of-darkness) as the canonical Lukan anchor of the doctrine of Satan-permitted-darkness-hour: the Passion proceeds not because Christ is defeated but because the Father permits the hour of the powers-of-darkness. The exousia tou skotous (authority of darkness) is the same authority Christ acknowledges at his arrest as permitted but not victorious. Tewahedo Holy-Week theology cites Lk 22:53 + Col 1:13 (delivered from the power of darkness) as the canonical doubled-witness for the doctrine that the Cross goes through the darkness-hour to the resurrection-light.

candidates.draft_body:
Cyril of Alexandria Commentary on Luke (c. 430 AD)

On Peter's Lukan-distinctive response after the cock-crow — 'And Peter went out, and wept bitterly' (Lk 22:62) — Cyril reads the eklausen pikrōs (wept bitterly) as the canonical Lukan anchor of the doctrine of repentant-tears as the active-receptive expression of post-fall sorrow: tears are not despair but the moisture of returning-love. Peter's tears are the inverse of Judas's hanging (Mt 27:5); the same betrayal, different response. Tewahedo penitential theology cites Lk 22:62 + 2 Cor 7:10 (godly sorrow worketh repentance) as the canonical doubled-witness for the doctrine of repentant-tears; the Tewahedo monastic 'gift of tears' (charisma of compunction) is the spiritual descendant of Peter's Lukan tears.
